title: Biggest and smallest
examples: Teacher, how do I know which is bigger?
Can we put these toys in order?

explain.say: Look at these two blocks. Say which one is bigger.
Now we have three pencils. We need to put them in order.
We can line up toys from smallest to biggest. This is putting them in order.
Look at these three animals. Which one is the biggest one?
When we line things up, we start with the smallest one first.
When you build with blocks, you must put them in order of size.

faq.q: How do I know which is bigger?
faq.a: You can compare the two things side by side. The one that takes up more space is bigger.
asks: How do I tell them apart?

faq.q: Do I always start with the smallest?
faq.a: When putting things in order, you usually start with the smallest one first. Then you go up to the biggest.
asks: Do I go up or down?

faq.q: Can I compare things that are not the same shape?
faq.a: Yes, you can compare shapes, as long as you are comparing their size. You just need to look at how big they seem.
asks: Does it matter what they are?

faq.q: What if the things are almost the same size?
faq.a: If they are very close, you can try to line them up carefully. One will still be just a tiny bit bigger.

faq.q: Is there a word for putting things in order?
faq.a: Yes, the word is 'order'. Putting things in order means lining them up from smallest to biggest, or vice versa.

facts: We compare two objects to see which is bigger or smaller.
Putting things in order means arranging them from smallest to biggest.
You can order things by size, weight, or height.
The smallest item is the one that takes up the least space.

quiz.say: Which is bigger: a pencil or a book?
quiz.why: A book usually takes up more space than a pencil.

wrong.0: This is wrong because we can easily see they are different sizes.
wrong.1: This is wrong because we are looking at typical sizes for comparison.
wrong.3: It is tempting to say pencil because it is a common object.

quiz.say: If we order small, medium, big, what comes after medium?
quiz.why: The order goes up in size, so after medium comes big.

wrong.0: This is a word, not the next size step.
wrong.2: This goes backward in size order.
wrong.3: This means the size did not change.

quiz.say: Which group is in order from smallest to biggest?
quiz.why: This list shows a clear, increasing order of size.

wrong.1: This is in reverse order, from biggest to smallest.
wrong.2: This jumps back to small before going to big.
wrong.3: This repeats a size instead of showing the next step.
